Docket No. ER26-3515-000
                                   UNITED STATES OF AMERICA
                                          BEFORE THE
                            FEDERAL ENERGY REGULATORY COMMISSION

PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.                                                            Docket No. ER26-3515-000


                MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE SUPPLEMENTAL COMMENTS AND
             SUPPLEMENTAL COMMENTS OF PERSISTENCE ANALYTICS GROUP LLC
           REGARDING VALIDATED PROJECT STATE, EVIDENTIARY CURRENCY, AND
                                  REVALIDATION

 I. MOTION FOR LEAVE TO FILE SUPPLEMENTAL COMMENTS
      Persistence Analytics Group LLC ("PAG") respectfully submits these supplemental comments concerning
 PJM Interconnection, L.L.C.'s proposed Interim Resource Adequacy Service ("IRAS") and Large Load
 Registry. PAG submitted initial comments in this docket on August 13, 2026. Those comments recommended,
 among other things, that material large-load information carry sufficient context to distinguish projected or
 requested load from more mature states, that execution-critical assumptions have identifiable revalidation
 triggers, and that material registry inputs preserve useful provenance and validation timing.
      Since PAG's initial filing, PJM has published implementation materials that provide materially greater
 detail about the Phase 1 Large Load Registry and the Bring Your Own New Capacity ("BYONC") validation
 process. Those materials include PJM's Large Load Registry Field Definitions and Examples, a BYONC Officer
 Certification Template, and an October 7, 2026 presentation describing the reporting and validation process for
 the 2029/30 Base Residual Auction.
      These materials could not have been addressed in PAG's August 13 comments and directly illuminate how
 several of the evidentiary issues raised there will be implemented. The supplemental comments are narrow,
 acknowledge the meaningful validation PJM has now established, and do not seek to delay the Phase 1 process
 or the upcoming auction. To the extent leave is required, PAG respectfully requests leave under Rule 212 of the
 Commission's Rules of Practice and Procedure, 18 C.F.R. § 385.212, because consideration of this limited
 update will assist the Commission without prejudice to any participant.
 II. PJM'S NEW MATERIALS ESTABLISH MEANINGFUL VALIDATION OF SPECIFIC
 PROPOSITIONS
     PJM's October 7 presentation describes Phase 1 as a temporary process used to determine the 2029/30
 Variable Resource Requirement curve adjustment for BYONC, with an enhanced process and tool to be
 developed based on experience and feedback for determining eligible IRAS for the 2027/28 Delivery Year and
 forward. PJM, Large Load Registry and BYONC Reporting Process for 2029/30 BRA, at 2 (Oct. 7, 2026).
      The new implementation materials provide more assurance than a reporting-only registry. An Electric
 Distribution Company ("EDC") submits the New Large Load and associated BYONC information, and PJM
 states that the relevant BYONC contract must be executed. Where an LSE submits directly, PJM instructs the
 LSE to obtain EDC confirmation of the New Large Load and provide that confirmation to PJM. Id. at 5.
      The Capacity Market Seller must separately provide an officer certification. The template states that PJM
 and PJM Settlement are relying on the certification as evidence that the participant has an executed contract with
 the specified New Large Load for the 2029/30 Delivery Year; the officer also certifies that the arrangement
 identified in Attachment A is true and accurate and that the underlying resource qualifies as BYONC under the
 applicable Tariff requirements. PJM, BYONC Officer Certification Template, Officer Certification &
 Attachment A (Oct. 2026).
      PJM then validates the registry information. For the large load, PJM checks for duplicates and uses EDC
 validation as needed. For BYONC, PJM verifies information against Capacity Exchange, ensures the resource
 meets Tariff criteria, checks for duplicates, and confirms submission of the executed-contract certification.
 PJM's determination of BYONC eligibility is then published in the Registry's BYONC Status field. PJM Oct. 7
 Presentation at 8.

                                                                                                Docket No. ER26-3515-000
     PAG supports those controls. They demonstrate that PJM is not treating every submitted representation as
self-proving. They also sharpen the remaining question: what proposition has been validated, and for what later
decision is that validation sufficient?
III. VALIDATION SHOULD IDENTIFY THE PROPOSITION VALIDATED
      A verified contractual relationship is decision-grade evidence of that contractual relationship; it
      is not necessarily decision-grade evidence of future energized or sustained demand.
    The current Registry field set appropriately identifies the customer, EDC interconnection request, location,
zone, business segment, 2026/27 and expected 2029/30 peak load, BYONC contract status, associated resource
identifiers, BYONC MW, submitter contacts, and PJM's BYONC Status. PJM, Large Load Registry Field
Definitions and Examples (Oct. 2026). Those fields are useful and substantially improve visibility.
     The field set does not, however, appear to contain a structured project-state field that distinguishes whether
the represented future load is reported or requested, contractually committed, executable, energized, or operating
on a persistent basis. Nor does the validation label itself distinguish whether PJM has validated identity and
duplicate status, an executed contractual relationship, Tariff eligibility, a forecast quantity, an executable project
state, or an operating state.
     That distinction matters because the same record can support different propositions with different degrees
of confidence. An executed BYONC contract may be sufficient evidence for a BYONC contractual or eligibility
determination while remaining insufficient, standing alone, to establish that the corresponding New Large Load
will energize on the represented schedule or sustain the represented demand.
    PAG therefore recommends that, as PJM develops the enhanced process, any material validation status
identify the proposition validated. PJM need not create a public scoring system or adopt PAG's terminology. A
concise status definition or associated metadata can make clear whether the validated fact concerns identity,
contract execution, Tariff eligibility, forecast state, project execution, operational capability, or another defined
proposition.
IV. EVIDENCE CURRENCY AND MATERIAL CHANGE SHOULD BE VISIBLE WHERE LATER
RELIANCE IS CONSEQUENTIAL
     The Registry contains submitter identity and contact information, but the current field definitions do not
appear to require an effective-as-of date for the underlying project-state evidence, a last-revalidated date, or a
structured material-change indicator for the large-load state itself. That omission becomes more important when
a validated record is reused for a different or later decision.
    PJM's implementation schedule illustrates the speed with which the information can become consequential.
The October 7 presentation shows the Phase 1 Registry closing on October 20, PJM finalizing validation on
November 14, planning parameters posting on November 19, and the Base Residual Auction opening on
December 9. PJM Oct. 7 Presentation at 3.
     PAG does not recommend continuous resubmission of unchanged data. It recommends that a material
validated state carry enough currency information to allow the relying entity to know when the relevant
evidence was effective or last materially confirmed. Where the represented MW, energization timing, customer
identity, EDC interconnection status, BYONC arrangement, resource status, or another fact supporting the
earlier determination changes materially, the affected determination should be revalidated before that prior
status is used as if nothing changed.
V. THE ENHANCED IRAS PROCESS IS THE APPROPRIATE PLACE TO MATCH EVIDENCE TO
THE DECISION
     PJM expressly characterizes Phase 1 as temporary and states that it will implement an enhanced process and
tool based on feedback and experience for eligible IRAS in later Delivery Years. That planned enhancement
provides a practical opportunity to preserve the distinction between a validated reported state and a state
sufficiently evidenced for a specific consequential decision.
     PAG does not ask the Commission to direct a new public scoring methodology, create a separate approval
layer, or displace PJM's technical judgment. Nor does PAG suggest that the current Phase 1 Registry must be
                                                        Page 2
                                                                                             Docket No. ER26-3515-000
redesigned before the 2029/30 auction. The narrow recommendation is that the evidentiary maturity of a
represented state be matched to the consequence of the decision for which PJM or another authorized entity
relies upon it.
      This can be implemented incrementally through status definitions, effective or validation dates, source
categories where useful, and material-change/revalidation indicators. The goal is not more data for its own sake.
It is to prevent a validated fact from being silently generalized beyond the proposition that the supporting
evidence actually establishes.
VI. REQUESTED COMMISSION RECOGNITION
    In light of PJM's new implementation materials, PAG respectfully recommends that the Commission
recognize the following principles as PJM completes Phase 1 and develops its enhanced Large Load Registry
and IRAS processes:
1. Validation should identify the proposition validated. A status showing that a contract, identity, duplicate
    check, or Tariff criterion has been validated should not be assumed to establish a more mature project or
    operating state unless the supporting evidence is suited to that proposition.
2. Material large-load states should preserve useful evidence currency. Where consequential reliance depends on
    a represented future state, the record should allow the relying entity to understand when the supporting
    evidence was effective or last materially validated.
3. Material change should trigger revalidation of the affected determination. Changes in represented MW,
    timing, customer or project identity, interconnection status, BYONC arrangement, resource status, or
    another decision-critical fact should not leave a prior validated state silently unchanged.
4. Evidence should be matched to the decision. Information sufficient for early planning visibility or a defined
    contractual determination may not be sufficient for an operational baseline, market parameter, infrastructure
    commitment, or other consequential reliance.
VII. CONCLUSION
     PJM's new implementation materials meaningfully strengthen the Large Load Registry by requiring EDC-
linked reporting, an executed BYONC contract, officer certification, duplicate checks, Tariff-eligibility review,
and PJM validation. PAG supports those controls.
     The remaining implementation issue is narrower but important: validation should make clear what has
actually been validated, how current that evidence is, and whether a material change requires the affected
determination to be revisited before continued reliance.
     Validation should identify the proposition validated. Evidence sufficient for one determination
     should not silently become evidence sufficient for every later decision.
     Recognizing these principles would build on PJM's current work, preserve implementation flexibility, and
improve the ability of PJM, state commissions, Electric Distributors, and other authorized users to distinguish a
validated reported state from a decision-reliance state.


Respectfully submitted,

Enclosed for filing in the above-captioned proceeding are the Motion for Leave to File Supplemental
Comments and Supplemental Comments of Persistence Analytics Group LLC regarding PJM
Interconnection, L.L.C.'s Large Load Registry and Bring Your Own New Capacity implementation
materials.
PAG's supplemental comments are limited to implementation issues raised by PJM's October 2026 materials,
including the distinction between the proposition actually validated, the currency of supporting evidence,
material-change revalidation, and the evidentiary maturity appropriate to later consequential reliance.
PAG does not seek to delay the Phase 1 Registry process or the 2029/30 Base Residual Auction and does not
propose a new public scoring methodology or separate approval layer.
